items.weakness_text: Severe computational inefficiency of the proposed method... solving only 500 instances on CVRP100 requires 7 days... training time omitted...
The contribution of this paper seems incremental... only difference is a different dual GCN module... idea of cross attention and gated fusion is standard... technical novelty unclear.
items.ac_evidence: About the contribution, the rebuttal improved the positioning and explained differences from DACT/N2S-type approaches, but for the more critical reviewers the contribution may still read as combining known components.

items.weakness_text: Evaluation is limited: no comparison with other encoding methods such as Synth-Att, NDS, L2Seg; lacks analysis of gating parameter alpha; fails to justify why two separate modalities are necessary.
items.ac_evidence: For missing comparisons to several strong recent baselines/encoders, the rebuttal provides reasons why some methods are not directly comparable, but it does not fully close the gap for reviewers who asked for broader head-to-head evidence.

items.weakness_text: Proposed method evaluated on limited scales (only 100 nodes) and only CVRP, failing to showcase broader applicability and robustness.

items.weakness_text: Practical value of the proposed method is questionable: GAMA 6.6 days vs DACT 33 minutes, 288x slower for marginal 0.26% improvement.

items.weakness_text: The method's primary contribution is fundamentally undermined by its prohibitive computational cost: GAMA requires 6.6 days of inference time to solve CVRP100 instances, 288‑fold increase compared to DACT, rendering the method unusable for any practical application.

The paper's claims of superior zero‑shot generalization are based on a flawed baseline comparison; the DACT baseline gap of 25.3% is inconsistent with previously published results, invalidating the claim of state‑of‑the‑art generalization.
